source.name: TITLE: Arroz Chaufa Recipe (Peruvian Fried Rice) | The Kitchn

ingredients: medium scallion whites (reserve the greens for the arroz chaufa)
neutral oil, such as vegetable or avocado
boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
pachikay (recipe above), divided, plus more as needed
medium red bell pepper, small-diced (1 cup)
medium scallion greens, thinly sliced, plus more for garnish
instructions: Process 5 medium scallion whites, 1 (2 1/2-inch) piece peeled and coarsely chopped ginger, and 16 peeled garlic cloves together in a mini food processor or blender, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed, until finely chopped. Transfer to a medium heatproof bowl and add 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt.

Heat 1/2 cup neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat until 375°F or shimmering and very tiny bubbles form on the bottom of the pan. Carefully pour over the scallion mixture (careful, it will sizzle up) and stir to combine. Let cool to room temperature, about 40 minutes.
Toss 1 3/4 pounds chopped boneless, skinless chicken thighs, 2 tablespoons of the dark soy sauce, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin together in a large bowl.

Heat a wok or large 12-inch cast iron skillet over high heat until almost smoking. Reduce the heat to medium high. Add half of the chicken and 1 1/2 teaspoons of the pachikay, and stir-fry until the chicken is cooked through and golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl.

Repeat cooking the remaining chicken with 1 1/2 teaspoons of the pachikay. Keep this chicken in the skillet. Add 1 small-diced medium red bell pepper and stir-fry until the pepper is crisp-tender, 1 to 2 minutes. Turn off the heat. Transfer to the bowl with the remaining chicken.

Wipe out the pan with paper towels and scrape up any browned or burned bits. Place back over medium-high heat. Add the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons pachikay and swirl the pan so the oil coats the bottom. Pour in 4 lightly beaten large eggs. Cook, stirring constantly, until the eggs are just scrambled and set, 20 to 30 seconds.

Add 1 1/2 teaspoons pachikay if the pan is dry. Add 4 cups day-old cooked jasmine rice. Stir-fry, tossing constantly and breaking up any clumps, until the rice grains are separated and heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and bell pepper mixture to the pan and stir-fry until heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium low. Drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons dark soy sauce and 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil, and toss to coat evenly. Add 5 thinly sliced medium scallion greens and 1 pinch MSG if desired, and toss to combine. Garnish with more thinly sliced scallion greens if desired.
Make ahead: The jasmine rice and pachikay can be made up to 4 days ahead and refrigerated in separate airtight containers.
